scenarios.title: Balance and clarification
turns: Could you tell me my current balance?
Sorry, could you say that a little more slowly?
Is that twelve hundred and fifty pounds, plus forty pence?
scenarios.review: Preserve the balance across turns; repeat clearly without sounding irritated.

scenarios.title: Remember a correction
turns: I'm thinking of sending fifteen pounds to Alex. Don't send anything yet.
Sorry, I meant fifty pounds, not fifteen. And the name is Alice, not Alex.
Before I decide, what amount and name did I settle on?
scenarios.review: Remember fifty pounds and Alice; do not claim a payment was made.

scenarios.title: Anxious caller
turns: I can't find my card and I'm worried someone might use it. What should I do?
If I freeze it and then find it, does that mean I need a new card?
I'm still a bit worried. Could you explain the first step simply?
scenarios.review: Give calm practical guidance; distinguish a temporary freeze from replacement.

scenarios.title: Sensitive conversation
turns: My dad died last week and I don't know where to start with his bank account.
This is quite hard to talk about. Can you keep it simple?
Would I be able to speak to someone who helps with this?
scenarios.review: Use restrained empathy and simple next steps; do not pretend a transfer has happened.

scenarios.title: Frustration and reassurance
turns: That forty-two pound payment failed again. This is really frustrating.
So have I been charged or not? I need a straight answer.
Okay. Just tell me what you know, without making promises.
scenarios.review: Clearly say no money was taken; do not invent a cause, repair or retry outcome.

scenarios.title: Conversation continuity
turns: Please call me Sam. I only want to understand freezing my card, not order a replacement.
Could you explain the difference in plain English?
What did I say I wanted to do, and what should you call me?
scenarios.review: Remember Sam and the stated preference; avoid unnecessary repetition.

limitations: Scripted synthetic caller, explicit turns where supported; no live barge-in or emotional-voice inference test. Caller audio is reused across providers and prompt conditions. Recordings preserve arrival gaps with simulated agent playout; latency is provider PCM arrival, not measured loudspeaker output. Provider transcripts are not independent accuracy verification. No tools or real banking actions are executed. Provider-specific prompts are documented starting configurations, not proven optimal tuning.
